home.heroText: Psychological rock and roll built on two bass guitars, drums and one unmistakable voice.
home.introText: BEAST came out of Cape Town in 2012 with a deliberately unusual setup: two bass guitars, drums and Inge Beckmann's voice. Heavy, raw and stripped of the usual lead-guitar architecture.

members.name: Inge Beckmann
members.bio: Frontwoman of Cape Town art-rock outfit Lark before its semi-permanent hiatus. Joined BEAST once the two-bass experiment 'sounded right', bringing a method-singing approach that swings between a whisper and a howl. She pushed for a name with an 'interesting visual effect' — Bow Beast — before the band settled on BEAST.

members.name: Rian Zietsman
members.bio: Guitarist of Taxi Violence who bought a bass with Louis Nel in late 2011 purely to learn the instrument. Plays the low, rhythmic end of the twin-bass setup, holding the floor while the second bass climbs over it.

members.name: Louis Nel
members.bio: Taxi Violence's drummer, turned bassist. Runs a higher, chord-based lead approach through a guitar amp — the reason BEAST sounds rawer and more low-fi than a standard rock four-piece.

members.name: Werner von Waltsleben
members.bio: Drummer of Afrikaans metal band Kobus!. A long-time fan of both Taxi Violence and Lark, he called joining BEAST 'a dream come true' — a chance to play the music he wanted to hear.

pastMember.name: Sasha Righini
pastMember.bio: Drummer of The Plastics, invited into the basement sessions early and soon a full member. Left in mid-2013 to pursue his own music.

band.instrumentation: The twin-bass setup is rare in South African music. Zietsman plays low and rhythmic like a normal bassist; Nel plays higher and chord-based like a lead guitarist, through a guitar amp. The result is rawer, harder and more low-fi than a standard four-piece.

timeline.title: The two-bass experiment begins
timeline.copy: Rian Zietsman and Louis Nel buy bass guitars and begin jamming in the basement of the house they share. Sasha Righini joins on drums and the project develops from an experiment into a band.

timeline.title: Kombass becomes BEAST
timeline.copy: The early working name Kombass gives way to BEAST after Inge Beckmann joins on vocals. The stripped setup is fixed: two bass guitars, drums and voice.

timeline.title: First Cape Town shows
timeline.copy: By May 2012 BEAST are being billed at The Assembly in Cape Town as a new supergroup featuring members of Lark, Taxi Violence and The Plastics.

timeline.title: Oppikoppi Sweet Thing
timeline.copy: BEAST join the 9–11 August Oppikoppi bill in Northam. Contemporary festival coverage later lists the band among the weekend highlights.

timeline.title: Smoke Swig Swear recorded
timeline.copy: The debut album is recorded over four days in September at Sound and Motion Studios in Cape Town, keeping the twin-bass sound raw and direct.

timeline.title: Rocking the Daisies
timeline.copy: BEAST play the sold-out Rocking the Daisies festival at Cloof Wine Estate in Darling during the 4–7 October weekend.

timeline.title: Synergy Live
timeline.copy: On 30 November BEAST play the main stage at Synergy Live at Theewaterskloof, scheduled 21:00–21:45 immediately before The Narrow and headliner The Prodigy.

timeline.title: Up the Creek
timeline.copy: On 1 February BEAST appear on Up the Creek's Friday-night Tribute to Women main-stage programme alongside SAARKIE, Tailor, Machineri and Karen Zoid.

timeline.title: Smoke Swig Swear launches
timeline.copy: The debut gets its official album launch at The Assembly in Cape Town on 23 February.

timeline.title: Design Indaba Music Circuit
timeline.copy: Four days after the album launch, BEAST play the Design Indaba Music Circuit at Aces n Spades as part of a three-day Cape Town programme spanning 32 artists and eight venues.

timeline.title: RAMfest
timeline.copy: BEAST are billed for RAMfest Cape Town, 7–10 March at Circle of Dreams near Riviersonderend, on a bill with Rise Against, Bring Me The Horizon and Pendulum.

timeline.title: The documentary and international press
timeline.copy: A short documentary follows the album launch, and on 28 August VICE/Noisey premieres the Smoke Swig Swear video alongside an interview with Inge Beckmann and the band's story.

timeline.title: Line-up change
timeline.copy: Sasha Righini leaves to pursue his own music and Werner von Waltsleben of Kobus! takes over on drums.

timeline.title: Crowdfunding Bardo
timeline.copy: On 13 August BEAST launch an Indiegogo campaign to fund album two while remaining unsigned and protecting their creative independence. A private investor later helps complete the record.

timeline.title: Private Bardo acoustic launch
timeline.copy: On 21 February, backers, family and friends attend an intimate acoustic launch at the Cape Town Club, with the material rearranged for a quieter setting.

timeline.title: Bardo launches publicly
timeline.copy: The second album receives its public launch on 27 February. Contemporary listings describe the record as the result of the band's 2014 fan-funded recording push.

timeline.title: Splashy Fen
timeline.copy: BEAST are announced for Splashy Fen's 2–6 April Easter-weekend edition near Underberg, joining a broad South African bill including Taxi Violence, Shortstraw, aKING and Nakhane Toure.

timeline.title: Critical peak for Bardo
timeline.copy: On 9 April the Mail & Guardian asks whether BEAST might be South Africa's finest live rock act, praising the force of the two-bass setup and Inge Beckmann's vocal range.

friends.name: Sedge Warbler
friends.careerSummary: Sedge Warbler was a Cape Town hip-hop/electronic duo: DJ Caviar and Expensive Drinks (also known as Dank). They described their sound as “EDM thug rap”, mixing sardonic MC-led vocals with broken electronic beats and glitch-hop production. Their 2010 release Welcome To The Universe captures the project's experimental approach and its place in Cape Town's early-2010s underground electronic scene.

careerSources.label: Penny Black Music — Welcome To The Universe
BEAST debut bill, The Assembly (2012)

friends.name: Counterstrike
friends.careerSummary: Counterstrike emerged from Cape Town's formative drum-and-bass scene, with Justin Scholtemeyer and Eaton Crous associated with the duo's early years. Their sound pushed from dark, high-energy drum and bass into crossbreed, neuro and industrial-leaning bass music. The project also helped build the scene through the Homegrown event series and Algorythm Recordings, and went on to play internationally.

careerSources.label: Resident Advisor — Counterstrike biography
Resident Advisor — artist profile

friends.name: The Future Primitives
friends.careerSummary: The Future Primitives are a Cape Town three-piece formed in late 2011, built around Johnny Tex, Heino Retief and Warren Fisher. Their analogue-minded sound draws on early rock 'n' roll, rockabilly, surf, 1960s garage and first-wave psychedelia. They recorded live to tape with minimal equipment and released This Here's The Future Primitives in 2012, followed by further releases in 2013.

careerSources.label: The Future Primitives — Bandcamp / debut album
The Future Primitives — music catalogue

friends.name: Rosemary Towns End
friends.careerSummary: Rosemary Towns End were a Cape Town rock 'n' roll trio comprising Cyle Myers, Jaryd Davidson and Asher Gamedze. The band built its identity around dirty guitar riffs, loose grooves and energetic live shows. Their documented release is the debut album Characters, issued in April 2013, placing them within the city's independent rock circuit of the early 2010s.

careerSources.label: Rosemary Towns End — Characters (2013)

friends.name: Haasbroek
friends.careerSummary: Haasbroek appears in contemporary listings for Cape Town's electronic and club-music circuit, including a multi-artist Assembly event in November 2011 and BEAST's debut bill in May 2012. The public material I could verify is event-based rather than a full artist biography, so this profile stays limited to those documented appearances rather than attaching an unverified identity or discography.

careerSources.label: The Assembly — November 2011 event archive
BEAST debut bill, The Assembly (2012)

friends.name: Sex on Decks
friends.careerSummary: Sex on Decks is documented on BEAST's 2012 Assembly bill and has a later release history in house and electronic music. The artist profile identifies Dan as a DJ and producer working across styles, with releases on independent house labels including Nurvous Records, Nite Grooves and Moiss Music. Its catalogue includes deep-house material as recently as 2026.

careerSources.label: Traxsource — Sex on Decks artist profile and releases
BEAST debut bill, The Assembly (2012)

friends.name: The Narrow
friends.careerSummary: The Narrow formed in 2002 and became one of South Africa's defining alternative-rock bands. Their debut Self Conscious (2003) earned a SAMA nomination; later records included Travellers, You Don't Get to Quit and Crocodiles. Their catalogue continued with Dangerous (2022) and two 2025 releases, Dying Heart and Euphoria, while the band retained its heavy, melodic live-rock identity.

careerSources.label: The Narrow — official band history and discography
B Sharp Entertainment — band interview and history

friends.name: The Prodigy
friends.careerSummary: The Prodigy formed in Braintree, Essex, in 1990 around producer and songwriter Liam Howlett. They helped move British rave and breakbeat into the mainstream with albums such as Experience and Music for the Jilted Generation, then became global chart leaders with The Fat of the Land and singles including Firestarter and Breathe. After Keith Flint's death in 2019, Liam Howlett and Maxim returned to touring in 2022.

careerSources.label: Official Charts — The Prodigy history and chart record
Insomniac — The Prodigy artist profile

friends.name: Karen Zoid
friends.careerSummary: Karen Zoid is a South African rock singer, songwriter and guitarist whose career began with the breakthrough album Poles Apart in 2001. Chasing the Sun followed in 2003, helping establish her as a major voice in local rock and Afrikaans music. Across albums including Media, Postmodern World, Terms & Conditions, Zoid Afrika and Drown Out the Noise, she has moved between English and Afrikaans songwriting and a long-running live career.

careerSources.label: HDS Entertainment — Karen Zoid biography and discography
MusicBrainz — Karen Zoid releases

friends.name: ISO
friends.careerSummary: ISO, formerly known as Isochronous, are a South African rock band formed in Pretoria in 2006. The group developed a melodic mix of rock, pop, electronic and dance influences. The 2012 album Piece by Piece marked the shortened name and a more structured, groove-oriented sound; earlier, Inscape had already signalled a shift from dark synth-rock toward progressive pop.

careerSources.label: The Citizen — Local band ISO beating the odds
IOL — ISO and Piece by Piece
Apple Music — Inscape by Isochronous

friends.name: YOAV
friends.careerSummary: YOAV is a Cape Town-born singer-songwriter known for a percussive guitar style that blends alternative songwriting with electronic and club textures. After moving between London and New York, he released the international debut Charmed & Strange in 2008, followed by A Foolproof Escape Plan and later releases including Blood Vine and Multiverse. In 2024 he collaborated with Jabulile Majola on the album Unyazi.

careerSources.label: AllMusic — YOAV biography
Coda Music — YOAV biography and releases

friends.name: Jeremy Loops
friends.careerSummary: Cape Town musician Jeremy Loops built a distinctive live sound around guitar, harmonica, vocals and looping pedals, drawing on folk, pop, soul and hip-hop. His debut album Trading Change (2014) opened the door to international touring; Critical as Water and Heard You Got Love followed. His 2025 album Feathers and Stone continues a career that has taken his loop-driven performances well beyond South Africa.

careerSources.label: Jeremy Loops — official website and latest album
AllMusic — Jeremy Loops biography

friends.name: Jakkals
friends.careerSummary: Jakkals were a Cape Town rock trio formed around James Boonzaier, Tim King and bassist Mark De Menezes. Their early sound blended rock bravado, pop melody and rhythmic, dance-leaning grooves. The group developed a following around venues such as The Assembly, The Waiting Room and Zula Bar, releasing the Trifle EP and singles including Woah! Nelly and Rum Trifle.

careerSources.label: Jakkals — artist biography and music
Bandsintown — Jakkals artist profile

friends.name: DJ Soosh
friends.careerSummary: Johannesburg DJ Soosh began DJing in 1997 and developed a reputation as a versatile open-format selector and turntablist. Rather than staying within one genre, his sets draw from hip-hop, funk, R&B, neo-soul, Motown, dancehall and drum and bass. His work spans clubs, festivals and corporate events, as well as live collaborations with South African and international performers.

careerSources.label: DJSA — DJ Soosh profile
Talent Hire — DJ Soosh biography and performance history

friends.name: St Fearless
friends.careerSummary: The name in the BEAST archive appears to refer to Saintfearless, a Cape Town rock band active around 2011–13. Contemporary profiles describe a five-piece built around Kieron Brown, Paul Fairbrother, Cody Meyer and twins Kevin and Kelvin Mercuur. The group campaigned for an Oppikoppi slot, headlined local festival bills and supported Van Coke Kartel, before appearing on the Up the Creek 2013 line-up.

careerSources.label: Saintfearless — 2011 band interview
Cape Town Music Scene — Saintfearless profile
Up the Creek 2013 line-up

friends.name: The Dollfins
friends.careerSummary: The Dollfins were a Cape Town trio in the city's garage, surf and punk scene in the early 2010s. A contemporary gig review described their sound as retro surf-punk and noted that two of the three members had also played in Beach Party. Their documented appearances include local club shows and support on the 2013 Dune Rats South African tour.

Built around blues-inflected, hard-edged rock, the group released Untie Yourself, The Turn, Unplugged: Long Way From Home, Soul Shake, Tenfold and Shape and Form I. They earned multiple SAMA nominations, toured locally and in Europe, and became known for high-energy festival performances.

friends.name: Rise Against

Their music pairs fast, aggressive arrangements with big choruses and socially conscious lyrics. Key releases include Siren Song of the Counter Culture, The Sufferer & the Witness and Appeal to Reason; their later catalogue includes Nowhere Generation and the 2025 album Ricochet.

friends.name: Bring Me The Horizon
friends.careerSummary: Bring Me The Horizon formed in Sheffield in 2004 and evolved from abrasive early metalcore into a genre-blending international rock act. Albums such as Sempiternal and That's the Spirit broadened their audience, while amo and the Post Human releases incorporated electronic, pop and experimental influences. The band have become major festival headliners, earning BRIT and Grammy nominations and selling millions of records worldwide.

His breakthrough came with the irreverent single Cooler as Ekke in 2009. Albums including Eksie Ou, Nag Van Die Lang Pette and Die Evangelie Van Goeie Tye helped establish his humour-driven style, distinctive persona and collaborations across South African music.

Later records include Real Rare Whale and If It Sucks, Turn It Up, with Old Mates arriving in 2026.
